Summer is one of the worst time for boxing fans, and though we had some amazing non-stop action from April to June, we're currently in a slump. Here are some fights until we reach August.

July 11

ESPN, Thurman-Collazo: Collazo a grizzled veteran, has had a decent career but got his ears boxed off by Khan in September. Thurman is a different beast to Thurman, to see if Collazo will benefit of the difference remains to be seen. Prediction: Thurman KO 8.

HBO Lationo, Herrera-Lundy: The unofficial light welterweight champion of the world returns, after two consecutive robberies, Herrera returns to face Hank Lundy. Lundy is a non-stop pressure fighter who'll look to break down Herrera. Fun fight. Prediction: Herrera UD.

beIN Sports Espanol, Donnie Nietes vs Fransisco Rodriguez: With guys like Estrada and Gonzales leaving the light flyweight division, there's a bit of a vacuum of who's the best fighter in the division. Donnie Nietes seeks to fill that empty spot at the otp of the division. Rodriguez hails from Mexico and also seeks the glory of being called the best at the division, this should be a decent fight at the very least between two guys at the world class level.

July 18

CBS, Frampton-Gonzales Jr:: There was a moment in life when the Super Bantamweight Division was one of the most interesting and competitive divisions in boxing, it all led by Nonito Donaire. Since 2013, the interest in the division has since then stemmed, may it be due to the lack of the big fights being made in the division, or the likes of Cruz and Donaire moving up is up for debate, but whatever it may be, the division is still quite interesting. Carl Frampton is one of the reasons for this, the British Frampton was one of the more promising prospects of the past few years, and his ascension to the world level has been unopposed. Some would say it's lack of opposition, other say he's just that good. Gonzales Jr ranks outside of the top 50, and won't give us an interesting fight. Just come to see Frampton, who's undoubtedly a talent.

Showtime, Chavez Jr, McJoe Arroyo: Chavez Jr returns, yes, that quick after getting demolished by Fonfara a few months ago. And he's up to his old tricks again, taking an opponent in Marcos Reyes, making him go up in weight and will likely outweigh him by 20ish pounds on fight night. There may be a chance for redemption in Chavez Jr, from what's been heard he's taking his training more seriously, personally I don't think jack shit will change, but hey who knows, what I do know is Marcos Reyes won't be the one to give Chavez Jr a shot a redeeming himself. In the undercard Puerto Rican McJoe Arroyo battles for the IBF Super Flyweight title, he faces Arthur Villanueva in a much higher level and much more important bout than Chavez-Reyes.

Unimas, Ik Yang vs Cesar Cuneca: If you don't know who Ik Yang is let me give a small choice of words to describe him to you: Provodnikov 0.5. Yeha, not 2.0, but 0.5. If you think Provodnikov was crude, Yang is raw. His level of technique is ridiculously low, he has no idea what a defense is, if he were a baseball player he'd pitch with no outfielders, or infielders...or catchers. He's an ultimate masochist who seems to laugh and smile every time he gets hit, but one of the rarest thing of him is how aggressive he is in the ring. To be honest he may be a masochist but he's also a sadist, he legitimately seems to enjoy punching people in the face. If guys like Pacquiao and Mayweather were pushed to boxing by hunger and poverty, Ik Yang got pushed to boxing by enjoying to get punched, and enjoying to punch.

Arthur Abraham vs Robert Stieglitz IV: I've no idea what to say about this fight even if I've watched all their three fights. Both are good fighters, past their best but still pretty good, it should make for another decent fight. I really have no idea what to say about this one.

Shumenov also fights against B.J Flores on the 25th, as does Kovalev.
Boxing in July: It's going to get better, I promise.

Tips to avoid a bad trip?

Make sure your mindset is positive and you don't have any big stressors going on.

Ensure that your setting is comfortable and free of any stress as well.

Having a good playlist of music is almost necessary.

Remember to hydrate before and during the trip.

If you find yourself thinking not-so-nice things, then try simply changing the music or the room you're in.

If you enjoy being on the PC, keep in mind that the TripSit org is available to give advice or whatever you need to make the trip go well. You dont need to be having a bad trip to join, but if you need quick advice be sure to hop into the chatroom.

The way I've done it is, go in knowing it's a drug (try not to forget you've taken it) and that you're in control. Obviously your control limitation is depending on how much you take but so far I've never had a bad trip.

When taking psychedelic drugs, I always find it very important to outline your expectations before the trip. Perhaps even more important than set and setting, even though expectations might be a part of the set.

Try to not have very high expectations, avoid reading trip reports as your trip definitely will feel totally different. Always be aware of the possibility of a bad trip, or being confronted by the weirdest thoughts or horrors. If you're aware that it might happen, it won't be so hard to handle if it actually does. I've tripped with people that never had experienced anxiety in their life, and who presumed a psychedelic trip would be only euphoria and sunshine. And when they did trip on for example LSD, they were so shocked by it not turning out as they expected that they felt out of place for days afterwards.
